source_conversation.content: I have an iPhone 15 and I want my photos backed up to iCloud so I don't lose them. How do I turn it on?

sections.text: On iPhone: 1. Open the Settings app and tap your name. 2. Tap 'iCloud', then tap 'iCloud Backup'. 3. Make sure 'Back Up This [Device]' is turned on. Conditions: Connect the device to a power source. Connect the device to a Wi-Fi network. Make sure the device's screen is locked. If you see an alert that you don't have enough iCloud storage, follow the onscreen steps to buy more storage.

On Android: 1. Open your device's Settings app. 2. Tap 'Google services', then 'All services'. Choose the data to back up: 'Photos & videos', 'Device data', or both. 3. Turn 'Backup' on. 'On' appears below each selected data type once the data is saved. Backup can't be used on a personal device set up with a work profile, a work-only device, or a company-owned device. Free backup storage is up to 15 GB. More storage is available through a Google One account. A Google One backup can take up to 24 hours.

source_conversation.content: I'm on an Android phone and I want to pair my new wireless earbuds. Where do I start?

sections.text: On Android: From the top of the screen, swipe down. Touch and hold Bluetooth. Tap Pair new device. If there's no Pair new device, check under Available devices, or tap More, then Refresh. Tap the name of the Bluetooth device. Follow the on-screen instructions. If you see a notification to pair, automatically connect your Bluetooth devices with Fast Pair. Some of these steps work only on Android 15 and up.

On Windows 11: Turn on the device and make it discoverable. The method depends on the device, so check its documentation or the manufacturer's website. On the taskbar, click the Network, Sound, or Battery icon next to the time and date. Select the Manage Bluetooth devices chevron on the Bluetooth quick setting, then select the device under New devices. If New devices doesn't appear, scroll through Your devices. Follow additional instructions if they appear, then select Done.

source_conversation.content: I have an iPhone 13 and I want to delete a game I never play called Candy Crush. How do I do it?

sections.text: On iPhone: Touch and hold the app. Tap 'Remove App.' Tap 'Delete App,' then tap 'Delete' to confirm. If you delete an app, it doesn't automatically cancel in-app subscriptions. If you don't see the option to delete an app, some built-in Apple apps can't be deleted. For third-party apps, check parental controls and make sure 'Deleting Apps' is set to 'Allow.' If an MDM solution manages the device, you may not be able to delete apps, so contact your administrator.

On Android: Launch the Play Store app. Tap your profile icon in the top-right corner. Tap 'Manage apps & devices,' then tap 'Manage.' Select the app you want to remove. Tap 'Uninstall.' Some of these steps work only on Android 13 and up. Supervised users can use some Personal Safety app features.

source_conversation.content: I'm on Windows 11 and I want to get rid of the Spotify app because I don't use it anymore. Can you walk me through it?

sections.text: On Windows 11: Open Start, go to 'All apps,' and search the list for the app. Press and hold the app, or right-click it, then choose 'Uninstall.' Open Start, then Settings, then Apps, then 'Installed apps.' Find the app, select 'More,' then choose 'Uninstall.' Some apps can't be uninstalled from the Settings app right now. For these, use the Control Panel method in the 'Uninstall from Control Panel' section. Apps built into Windows can't be uninstalled, so you may not see an Uninstall option for them.

On Mac: Quit the app first. If the app is currently open, quit the app before continuing. Locate it in the Applications folder, or use Spotlight with Command (⌘) and double-click. If the app isn't made by Apple, find out whether it includes an 'Uninstall' or 'Uninstaller' app. If the app doesn't include an uninstall app or feature, drag the app to the Trash. If you're asked for a user name and password, enter the name and password of an administrator account on your Mac. To permanently delete the app and make its storage space available for other items, choose Finder > Empty Trash. You can't use the Finder to delete apps that are required by your Mac. If you can't delete an app because your Mac says that it's in use, make sure that the app isn't open.

sections.text: On iPhone: Open the Health app and tap the Summary tab. Tap your profile picture in the upper corner. Under your profile picture, tap 'Medical ID'. Turn on 'Show When Locked' to make Medical ID available from the Lock screen. Tap 'Edit' or 'Add' next to a field to update it. You can add medications, allergies, and conditions. Tap 'Done'.

On iPhone: To share your Medical ID with emergency responders, turn on 'Share During Emergency Call'. Medical ID is then shared automatically when you call or text emergency services from iPhone or Apple Watch. If you turn off 'Emergency Calls & SOS', your Medical ID information will not be shared. This is set under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services.

On Android: Open the Safety app and sign in to your Google Account. Tap 'Your info'. Tap 'Medical information', then tap an item such as blood type, allergies, or medications to update it. For contacts, tap 'Emergency contacts' and then 'Add contact'. Choose the existing contact you want to add. To show your emergency information when your screen is locked, tap 'Emergency info access' and then 'Show when locked'.

source_conversation.content: My iPhone is missing and I think I left it on the train. I have my iPad with me. How do I mark my iPhone as lost in Find My?

sections.text: On iPhone: Use the Find My app on another device or a Family Sharing group member's device. 1. In the Find My app, go to the Devices tab. 2. Scroll down and select your missing iPhone or iPad. 3. Tap the More button. 4. Scroll down to 'Lost [Device]', then turn on 'Lost Mode'. 5. Follow the onscreen steps if you want to display your contact information on your missing device. 6. Tap 'Activate'.

On iPhone: If the device is off or offline, it only appears online and in Lost Mode if the device has been turned on and is connected to Wi-Fi or cellular. If Stolen Device Protection is on for iPhone, Face ID or Touch ID is required to turn off Lost Mode, even if someone knows your passcode. If Find My wasn't on before the loss, you can't mark the device as lost or remotely erase it.

On Android: 1. Open the Find Hub app on another Android phone or tablet, or use Find Hub in a browser. 2. Sign in, then select the lost device. 3. Select 'Play sound'. It rings the device at full volume for 5 minutes, even on silent or vibrate.

sections.text: On iPhone: 1. Make sure that iOS or iPadOS is up to date. 2. Open the Settings app. 3. Tap Accessibility, then tap Hearing Devices. 4. Tap Pair MFi Hearing Device, then follow the onscreen instructions. You'll be asked to select your available hearing device, then tap Pair. If you don't see Pair MFi Hearing Device, tap the name of your hearing device when it appears in Hearing Devices settings. Then tap Pair when you see one or more Bluetooth pairing requests.

On Android: 1. From the top of the screen, swipe down. 2. Touch and hold Bluetooth. 3. Tap Pair new device. If there's no Pair new device, check under Available devices or tap More, then Refresh. 4. To pair your device, tap the name of the Bluetooth device. 5. Follow the on-screen instructions. If you're asked for a passcode and don't have it, try the most common ones like 0000 or 1234. Some of these steps work only on Android 15 and up.

sections.text: On iPhone: On your iPhone or iPad, open the App Store. Browse the Today, Games, Apps, or Arcade tabs, or tap the Search tab to look for a specific app. Tap the price or Get button. If you see the Open button instead, you already bought or downloaded the app. You might need to enter your Apple Account password to complete the download. Confirm the purchase by double-clicking the side button on your iPhone. With Face ID, glance at the device. With Touch ID, rest your finger on the button. An app with a Get button instead of a price is free, and you won't be charged to download it. Free apps may offer in-app purchases and subscriptions.

On Android: Open Google Play. On a phone or tablet, use the Play Store app. Find the app you want. Check the app's reliability. Under the app's title, look at its star ratings and number of downloads. To read individual reviews, scroll to the 'Ratings and reviews' section. When you choose an app, tap 'Install' for free apps, or tap the app's price for paid apps. Some of these steps work only on Android 8.0 and up.

source_conversation.content: I accidentally deleted an email with my class schedule in it yesterday. I'm using Gmail on my computer. How do I get it back?

sections.text: On Gmail on a computer: Go to Gmail on your computer. On the left, click 'More', then 'Trash'. Check the box to the left of each message you want to recover. At the top, click 'Move to'. In the 'Move to' menu, choose the folder where you want the messages to go, such as your inbox. When you delete a message in Gmail, it's moved to Trash. Up to 30 days after deletion, you can find the message in Trash. After 30 days, the message is permanently deleted and can't be recovered. Deleted drafts can't be recovered from Trash.

On Outlook.com: Open the Deleted Items folder and check whether the message is there. If it is, select the message and select 'Restore'. If the message isn't in Deleted Items, open that folder. Above the message list, select 'Recover items deleted from this folder'. If you find the message, select it and then select 'Restore'. Messages removed from the Deleted Items folder are recoverable for 30 days.

Drag the corners to adjust the scan to fit the page, then tap Keep Scan. Tap the Done button, or add more scans to the document. In iOS 26, you can also select options such as flash or an image filter. Alternatively, in an open note, tap the More button, then tap Scan.

On iPhone: In the Files app, tap the More button. Tap Scan Documents. Position the document in front of the camera. If your device is in Auto mode, your document will automatically scan. sections.text: On iPhone: Open Settings, tap Apps, then tap Phone. Choose how to handle calls from numbers not saved in your contacts. Scroll to Screen Unknown Callers and select one of three options. Never: Calls from unsaved numbers ring like any other call. Ask Reason for Calling: Calls are screened. The caller is asked why they're calling before your phone rings. Silence: Calls are silenced and sent to voicemail. Call screening may incur standard calling and data rates. On iOS versions earlier than iOS 17, Live Voicemail must also be turned on to use call screening. While roaming, calls are not screened, regardless of settings. If you call emergency services, call screening turns off for 24 hours.

sections.text: On iPhone with iOS 17.3 or later: Open Settings and select 'Face ID & Passcode'. Enter your device passcode. Select 'Stolen Device Protection', then switch it on or off.

On iPhone with iOS 17.3 or later: The extra measures are required only when your iPhone is away from familiar locations. To require them everywhere, go to Settings, tap 'Face ID & Passcode', then tap 'Stolen Device Protection' and choose 'Always' under 'Require Security Delay'. With this option, updates to certain security settings always require a delay, and biometric-only actions apply even if you are in a familiar location like home or work.

On Android: Open your device's Settings app. Tap 'Google', then 'All services'. Under 'Personal & device safety', tap 'Theft protection'. Theft protection is not supported on Android Go devices, tablets, or wearables. You must set a screen lock (PIN, pattern, or password) first.

sections.text: On iPhone: 1. Open the Settings app. 2. Tap your name at the top, then select 'Sign-In & Security.' 3. Turn on 'Turn on two-factor authentication' and complete the prompts that appear. Most accounts already use two-factor authentication, so you may not need to enable it. If your Apple Account was created with two-factor authentication, the protection can't be removed.

On a computer: 1. Go to myaccount.google.com. 2. Tap 'Security & sign-in.' 3. Under 'How you sign in to Google,' choose 'Turn on 2-Step Verification.' 4. Complete the prompts that appear. If the account is managed through work, school, or another group, these steps may not work. Contact your administrator.

sections.text: On Gmail on a computer: On your computer, open Gmail. Review the sender's messages before unsubscribing. In the left menu, click 'More', then 'Manage subscriptions'. On the right, next to the number of recent emails from that sender, click 'Unsubscribe'. Gmail unsubscribes you from all active mailing lists related to the sender. The sender may take a few days to process the request, so you may still receive emails during that time. New emails from the unsubscribed sender go to Spam, with a banner explaining why. Some senders send you to their website. If a pop-up appears, click 'Go to website' to unsubscribe there, or 'Block instead' to block the sender. Blocking a sender does not unsubscribe you from their mailing list. Their future emails go directly to Spam. The ability to manage email subscriptions is gradually rolling out and may not be available to you yet.

sections.text: On iPhone: Open Settings and select 'Wi-Fi', then switch Wi-Fi on. The phone automatically searches for nearby networks. Select the network you want. You may first need to enter its password or accept its terms and conditions. If you don't know the password, ask your network administrator. Check for a blue tick beside the network name and the Wi-Fi icon in the top corner of the screen. This confirms the connection. Optional: For a more reliable connection that uses cellular data alongside Wi-Fi, scroll down and turn on 'Connectivity Assist.'

On Android: Open the Settings app. Tap 'Network & internet', then 'Internet'. Tap a listed network. Networks with a lock icon require a password. If the network is nearby but not listed, wait for the list to refresh. If the network still isn't listed, scroll to the bottom and tap 'Add network'. Enter the network name (SSID) and security details, then tap 'Save'. Hidden network: Tap 'Advanced options', set 'Hidden Network' to 'Yes', then tap 'Save'.

sections.text: On Windows 11: Select the Network, Sound, or Battery icons on the taskbar to open Quick Settings. A Disconnected icon appears when you're not connected. In the Wi-Fi quick setting, select 'Manage Wi-Fi connections'. Choose the Wi-Fi network you want, then select 'Connect'. If the network you expect isn't listed, select the 'Refresh network list' button in the lower right to start a new scan. If prompted, type the network password, then select 'Next'.

sections.text: On Samsung Galaxy: Open Settings and tap 'Connections'. Tap 'Wi-Fi'. Turn on the Wi-Fi toggle if it's off. Wi-Fi must be activated to see available networks. Tap the name of the network you want. If the network is password-protected, enter the password and tap 'Connect'. A password-protected network requires you to have its password first. When connected, the network name appears under 'Current network', with 'Connected' below it.
